problem: Existing VLN methods usually encode only the immediate past time step (e.g., a recurrent state or the previous action/view), which is insufficient to capture long-term temporal context and navigation progress.
motivation: Historical navigation memory indicates how far the agent has progressed along the instruction. Modeling long-range dependencies over the trajectory should help the agent ground instructions and make better decisions. Only the abstract was available, so details are limited.
key_idea: A Transformer with a global historical context memory that adaptively selects the most relevant past episodes and encodes them as global memory to model long-term dependencies.
insight: Per the abstract, adaptively selecting relevant history rather than relying only on the last step improves SR/SPL on R2R, with larger gains in seen environments (+3.7 SR, +3.3 SPL) than unseen (+2.2 SR, +0.83 SPL). No ablations are available in the abstract, so the causal attribution is unverified.
method: Global historical context memory: stores representations of past navigation steps/episodes over the whole trajectory
Adaptive episode selection: selects the most relevant historical episodes for the current decision
Global memory encoding: encodes the selected history within a Transformer to model long-term dependencies
Transformer VLN policy: fuses instruction, current observation and global memory to predict actions

setting.backbone: Transformer-based VLN network (details not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: R2R dataset (details not given in abstract)

results: On R2R, the model improves over its baseline by an absolute 3.7% SR and 3.3% SPL in seen environments, and by 2.2% SR and 0.83% SPL in novel environments. The baseline is not named in the abstract.
